title: Maximum Of Absolute Value Expression
description:
Given two arrays of integers with equal lengths, return the maximum value of:\r
\r
|arr1[i] - arr1[j]| + |arr2[i] - arr2[j]| + |i - j|\r
\r
where the maximum is taken over all 0 <= i, j < arr1.length.\r

 
Example 1:

Input: arr1 = [1,2,3,4], arr2 = [-1,4,5,6]
Output: 13

Example 2:

Input: arr1 = [1,-2,-5,0,10], arr2 = [0,-2,-1,-7,-4]
Output: 20

 
Constraints:

2 <= arr1.length == arr2.length <= 40000
-10^6 <= arr1[i], arr2[i] <= 10^6

def check(candidate):
    assert candidate(arr1 = [1, 2, 3, 4], arr2 = [-1, 4, 5, 6]) == 13
    assert candidate(arr1 = [1, -2, -5, 0, 10], arr2 = [0, -2, -1, -7, -4]) == 20
    assert candidate(arr1 = [0], arr2 = [0]) == 0
    assert candidate(arr1 = [1, 1, 1], arr2 = [1, 1, 1]) == 2
    assert candidate(arr1 = [1, 2], arr2 = [3, 4]) == 3
    assert candidate(arr1 = [-5, -2, 0, 3], arr2 = [4, -1, 2, 8]) == 16
    assert candidate(arr1 = [10, -10, 10, -10], arr2 = [5, 5, -5, -5]) == 33
    assert candidate(arr1 = [1, 3, 6, 10], arr2 = [2, 4, 8, 16]) == 26
    assert candidate(arr1 = [7, 7, 7, 7, 7], arr2 = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == 8
